findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset
findings.body: The migration always does execute(...embed_category...)[0]['id'] and, if that is 0, execute(...uncategorized_category_id...)[0]['value']. Both settings are optional: embed_category is usually absent, and uncategorized_category_id is a hidden default that often has no site_settings row. An empty result makes [0] nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError and cannot be applied on a normal site.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and will not match
findings.body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with raw SQL, skipping EmbeddableHost's before_validation stripping of scheme and path. record_for_host/host_allowed? compare URI#host (hostname only) to the stored column, so values previously saved as http://example.com or https://example.com/path no longer match and embedding breaks after upgrade. The same interpolation of '#{h}' is also not quoted, so a host containing a quote aborts the migration or injects SQL.

findings.title: Host allow-list lookup is case-sensitive on the parameter
findings.body: record_for_host queries lower(host) = ? but passes uri.host unchanged. Ruby's URI does not downcase the host, so a referer or embed URL like http://EvilTrout.com looks up lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com' and fails even when the stored host is eviltrout.com. That rejects legitimate embeds and topic retrieval.

findings.title: Nil or port-bearing hosts cannot be saved or matched
findings.body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without a nil guard, so create/update with a missing host raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error. The format regex also allows a port (example.com:3000), but host_allowed? compares only URI#host, which drops the port, so a saved host that includes a port never matches the referer.

findings.title: Missing host update/destroy returns 500
findings.body: update and destroy load EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call save_host(host) or host.destroy. A bad id yields nil and a NoMethodError (500) instead of a 404. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present.

findings.title: No uniqueness on host makes category assignment nondeterministic
findings.body: embeddable_hosts has no unique index on host, and the model does not validate uniqueness. record_for_host uses an unordered .first, so two rows for the same host can assign imported embed topics to different categories depending on which row the database returns. Duplicate allowed hosts are also possible from the admin UI.
